title: The Duel
novel:
Two [[ancient|ancient]] [[swords|sword]] had hung on the living-room wall since the day Ted and Marshall signed the [[lease|lease]].

One of them was [[inherited|inherit]] from Ted's grandfather. The other Marshall bought at a market. Neither man could prove [[ownership|ownership]] of the flat itself, and now Lily was moving in.

The [[tension|tension]] grew all week. It began as a small [[dispute|dispute]] about a bookshelf and turned into a [[furious|furious]] argument about the future.

"If you two [[split up|split up]]," Ted said, "where do I live?"

Marshall lifted a [[blade|blade]] and [[threatened|threaten]] him, joking. Ted lifted the other. They were both [[clumsy|clumsy]] and neither had held a real weapon before.

It was, everyone agreed later, [[symbolic|symbolic]]: two friends fighting over a home that belonged to their childhood.

Then Ted [[accidentally|accidentally]] [[stabbed|stab]] Marshall's hand.

There was blood, a [[bandage|bandage]], a taxi, and four [[stitches|stitches]]. The [[wound|wound]] was small; the shame was large.

In the hospital they called a [[truce|truce]] and reached a quiet [[compromise|compromise]]: the flat would stay in the family, whatever the family became.

The swords went into a cupboard, where dangerous [[symbols|symbol]] belong.

lease.en: a written agreement to rent a flat or house

inherit.en: to receive money or things from someone after they die

tension.en: a feeling that people may start to fight or argue

split up.en: to end a relationship and separate

blade.en: the flat sharp part of a knife or sword

threaten.en: to say you will hurt someone or cause trouble

clumsy.en: moving badly and often dropping or breaking things

stab.en: to push a knife into someone

bandage.en: a long piece of cloth you wrap around a hurt part of the body

stitches.en: the thread a doctor uses to close a cut in your skin

wound.en: an injury where the skin is cut or broken

truce.en: an agreement to stop fighting for a while

compromise.en: an agreement where each side gives up a little

symbol.en: a thing that represents a bigger idea
